nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › How blue-green works § group#0

content.label: How blue-green works
content.takeaway: Blue-green deployment uses two identical environments for seamless, low-risk releases and rollbacks.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › How blue-green works § text#0

content.markdown: You keep two identical production environments, called blue and green. One of them serves all live traffic while the other sits idle¹; you deploy the new version to the idle one, test it there, and then move traffic over in one step². Because the old environment is still running, going back is the same one-step switch³. The cost is running twice the infrastructure during a release, which is why the idle environment is scaled down between releases⁴.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › How blue-green works § text#1

content.markdown:
¹ The idle environment is not serving live traffic.
² Traffic is switched in a single step after deployment and testing.
³ Reverting to the old version is a quick, single-step process.
⁴ To mitigate cost, the idle environment is scaled down when not in use.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § group#0

content.label: Before you start
content.takeaway: Ensure all prerequisites are met for a smooth blue/green deployment.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § text#0

content.markdown: You need the following in place before the first release:

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § text#1

content.markdown:
- Two identical environments, `orders-blue` and `orders-green`, with the same instance count, instance size and configuration.
- A health endpoint, `GET /healthz`, that returns `200` only when the service can reach its database and its queue.
- Database migrations that are backward compatible, so the old version keeps working against the new schema. This is a hard requirement: both versions share one database, and a rollback does not undo a migration.
- Access to the load balancer's listener rules, because the switch is a change to which target group the listener forwards to.
- A dashboard or query that shows the 5xx error rate per environment, so you can tell green's errors from blue's.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § text#2

content.markdown: If any migration is not backward compatible, do not use this procedure; split the migration into an additive release first and a cleanup release later.

nodes.title: Prerequisites for Release
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § text#3

content.markdown: This section outlines the essential prerequisites for a successful release using the blue/green deployment strategy. Key requirements include identical environments, a robust health check, backward-compatible database migrations, load balancer access, and error rate monitoring.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § group#0

content.label: Steps
content.takeaway: Blue/green deployment with rollback ensures zero-downtime and minimal customer impact.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#0

content.markdown: In this walkthrough blue is live and green is idle.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § step#1
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#1

content.markdown: Deploy version `2.8.0` to `orders-green`, using the same build artifact that passed staging rather than a fresh build. Expected result: all green instances report the new version, and blue still serves 100% of traffic.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § step#2
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#2

content.markdown: Apply the database migrations from the new release, once, from a single job rather than from every green instance at startup. Expected result: the migration job exits with code 0, and blue keeps serving requests without new errors, which confirms the change is backward compatible.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § step#3
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#3

content.markdown: Poll the health endpoint on every green instance until all of them return `200`. If any instance is still failing health checks after 10 minutes, stop here and roll back: tear down green and leave blue serving traffic. Nothing has been switched yet, so customers are unaffected.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § step#4
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#4

content.markdown: Send the smoke-test suite to green's internal address. Expected result: all smoke tests pass. If one fails, treat it like a failed health check and stop.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § step#5
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#5

content.markdown: Point the listener at the green target group. Expected result: within about 30 seconds, new requests are served by green, and blue receives no new connections.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § code#0
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § step#6
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#6

content.markdown: Observe the 5xx error rate on green for 15 minutes after the switch. If the error rate rises above 2% at any point in that window, switch back: run the same command with `$BLUE_TG_ARN`, which returns all traffic to blue within about 30 seconds. If it stays at or below 2%, continue.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § step#7
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#7

content.markdown: Leave blue running, unchanged, for 24 hours. It is your rollback target until then.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § step#8
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#8

content.markdown: After 24 hours without a switch-back, scale blue down. Blue becomes the idle environment for the next release, with the roles reversed.

nodes.title: Rollback Condition
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#9

content.markdown: If any green instance fails health checks after 10 minutes, roll back by tearing down green. Customers are unaffected.

nodes.title: Rollback Condition
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#10

content.markdown: If any smoke test fails, roll back by tearing down green. Customers are unaffected.

nodes.title: Rollback Condition
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#11

content.markdown: If the 5xx error rate on green rises above 2% within 15 minutes after the switch, switch traffic back to blue.

nodes.title: Outcome
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#12

content.markdown: This blue/green deployment strategy allows for zero-downtime deployments with immediate rollback capabilities.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong § group#0

content.label: When things go wrong
content.takeaway: Rollbacks are cheap before customer exposure, but database compatibility is crucial for safe recovery.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong § rollback_considerations

content.markdown: A rollback before step 5 is cheap, because customers never saw green. A switch-back after step 5 is also fast, but requests that were in flight on green during the switch may fail and need a client retry. Neither kind of rollback reverts the database, which is why the backward-compatible migration requirement matters. Whichever way you roll back, record what failed before trying again, because a second attempt with the same build tends to fail the same way.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong § migration_warning

content.markdown: Do not run the next release's migrations while blue is still on standby. If you do, the standby may no longer work against the schema, and the switch-back stops being a safe option.

nodes.title: Rollback Implications
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong § text#0

content.markdown: This section highlights the implications of rollbacks at different stages of deployment and emphasizes the importance of backward-compatible database migrations. It also warns against running future migrations on a standby environment.
